chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad bin Khalid al-Ash’ari, from Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Ash’ari, from Tha’laba bin Maimoun, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Hamran bin A’yan, that he said: I asked Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) about the apparent of the Qur’an and its inside.

He said: Its apparent applies to those for whose sake the Qur’an was revealed, and its inside applies to those who act by the same deeds of theirs; it continues in them what was revealed for the sake of those.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, the fourth Imam, known for his deep knowledge of the Qur'an.
key_terms.بَطْنُ الْقُرْآنِ: The inner or esoteric aspect of the Qur'an, referring to those who emulate the original recipients and share in their spiritual status.
key_terms.ظَهْرُ الْقُرْآنِ: The apparent or outer aspect of the Qur'an, referring to the specific context or people of revelation.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the apparent and inner meanings of the Qur'an according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the hermeneutical principle of *zahr* (apparent) and *batn* (inner) by linking the original recipients of revelation to those who emulate their conduct. This establishes a dynamic continuity in divine law, where the 'inner' meaning is not merely esoteric but practical, extending the specific rulings of the initial context to later generations who mirror their actions. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on the living application of the Qur’an through the example of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful.
